<problem>
For each even integer \(n\ge 2\), let \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For every ordered pair \(i\ne j\) in \([n]\), draw \(U_{ij}\) independently from the uniform distribution on \([0,1]\). Participant \(i\) prefers \(j\) to \(k\) exactly when \(U_{ij}<U_{ik}\); these preferences are strict with probability one.

A perfect matching is a map \(M:[n]\to[n]\) satisfying \(M(M(i))=i\) and \(M(i)\ne i\) for every \(i\). It is stable if there are no distinct participants \(i,j\), with \(j\ne M(i)\), for which both
\[
U_{ij}<U_{i,M(i)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
U_{ji}<U_{j,M(j)}.
\]
Let \(P_n\) be the probability that at least one stable perfect matching exists. Determine the exact ordered pair \((\alpha,C)\in(0,\infty)^2\) such that
\[
\lim_{\substack{n\to\infty\\ n\text{ even}}} n^{\alpha}P_n=C.
\]
</problem>

12	## 1. The finite stable-permutation sieve
13	
14	For a permutation \(\sigma\) without fixed points, call \(\sigma\) stable if
15	
16	1. every participant weakly prefers its successor \(\sigma(i)\) to its predecessor \(\sigma^{-1}(i)\);
17	2. no pair \(i,j\) both strictly prefer each other to their respective predecessors.
18	
19	For a 2-cycle, the first condition is automatic. A stable permutation consisting entirely of 2-cycles is precisely a stable perfect matching.

21	We use the following exact, finite combinatorial theorem, usually called the stable-permutation inclusion–exclusion theorem or sieve.

23	**Stable-permutation sieve.** For every strict preference profile,
24	\[
25	\mathbf 1_{\{\text{a stable perfect matching exists}\}}
26	=
27	\sum_{\substack{\sigma:\ \text{all cycles even}\\
28	                         \text{all cycles have length }\ge2}}
29	(-1)^{c_{\ge4}(\sigma)}
30	\mathbf 1_{\{\sigma\text{ is stable}\}},

35	This is the classical finite identity underlying Mertens’s inclusion–exclusion formula. In particular, the sign is one minus sign **per long cycle**, not per vertex. We will need substantial cancellation in this identity.

60	\int_{[0,1]^n}
61	\left(\prod_{i\text{ in long cycles}}x_i\right)
62	\prod_{\{i,j\}\notin E_\sigma}(1-x_ix_j)\,d\boldsymbol x.
63	\tag{3}
64	\]
